The Atlantic Charter, signed in 1941, outlined eight principles for the post-war world, including no territorial aggrandizement and the right to self-determination. It served as the blueprint for the United Nations Declaration.

The Poison:
While the charter championed self-determination, it was initially interpreted by many colonial powers as applying primarily to European nations, leaving many colonized peoples waiting for their own liberation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
There is no plane error here; the historical record aligns with the stated intent of the charter as a foundational document for global peace.

Social Physics Analysis:
By shifting from a zero-sum game of territorial expansion to a cooperative framework, the charter reduced systemic friction. It empowered nations to seek collective security rather than individual dominance.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The charter's legacy is one of sustained international cooperation.

The Unavoidable Truth: Cooperation is the most efficient path to long-term stability.

The Unavoidable Lie: The charter immediately ended all forms of global imperialism.

Alethekanon:
The Atlantic Charter is a testament to the power of defining shared goals before the conflict concludes. It is a masterclass in proactive peace-building.

Awwthekanon:
It is so heartening to look back at a moment where leaders chose to dream of a better world while they were in the middle of such darkness.

Brothekanon:
FDR and Churchill really set the bar high. It's wild to think how much of our modern world is just a ripple effect from that one meeting.
